criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (or the drain.rs unit tests) lands a job whose diff adds an unknown key to athena.toml; `cargo test -p athena-cli` passes, the test asserts the job's recorded outcome is landed (not failed), and the report's stop is not Stop::RepeatedFailure.
criteria.evidence: I ran two new tests and both passed. The real-steps test `a_landing_whose_config_the_running_build_cannot_read_is_recorded_landed_and_ends_with_reinstall` uses a ConfigLander that commits athena.toml with `[brand_new_section] new_key = 1`. It checks that JobConfig::at(head) really fails with the production strict parser, that the Records state is `JobState::Closed(OutcomeState::Landed)`, that the stop is NeedsReinstall, and that failed_item is None. The stub test also asserts `assert_ne!(report.stop, Stop::RepeatedFailure)` and that the job line reads passed/landed. The full suite passed in Athena's recorded CI run.

criteria.criterion: In that test the run's final report/output contains a note telling the user to reinstall, and the run ends cleanly (no failure counted for the item); checked by `cargo test -p athena-cli`.
criteria.evidence: Both tests check that `display::drain(&report)` contains `stopped     reinstall needed`. They check that report.notes has a note containing `Reinstall Athena` and `athena drain`, and the stub test also requires the parse error text in it. They check that no job line is failed, rejected or no outcome, and that the text has no `repeated failure` or `failed twice`. The stub log is exactly [read a, run a, land a], so the job was not rated and the second item did not run. display.rs prints report.notes (lines 604 and 718).

criteria.criterion: A regression test shows a genuine failure (job that does not land twice) still ends with Stop::RepeatedFailure; `cargo test -p athena-cli` passes.
criteria.evidence: The new test `a_job_that_does_not_land_twice_still_ends_as_repeated_failure_when_the_config_is_readable` uses `unlandable: vec!["a"]` and asserts Stop::RepeatedFailure with failed_item Some("a") and no `reinstall` in the output. It passed, and so did the two existing repeated-failure tests.

criteria.criterion: The change touches only files under crates/athena-core/src/run/, crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs, its stop display text, and their tests (git diff --stat), plus CHANGELOG.md.
criteria.evidence: `git diff --stat HEAD~1` lists only CHANGELOG.md, crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs, crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs (the drain --help stop list) and crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs. All four are on the expected deliverables list. The planned changes to display.rs and run/ were not needed: display already renders the stop label and notes, and the fault is in the drain.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has a new entry describing that a landed config the running build cannot parse ends the run cleanly with a reinstall note instead of a false repeated failure.
criteria.evidence: A new bullet under `### Fixed` (Unreleased) says that `athena drain` no longer ends with a false `repeated failure` when a landing adds a key the running build does not know. It says the job is recorded as landed, the run ends with `reinstall needed` and no failure counted, the note says to reinstall (`./setup.sh`) and run `athena drain` again, and the rebuilt case ends as `rebuilt`. It also names the root cause.

criteria.criterion: `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass (tested default).
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks for 806666120f7d all passed (CI run 41573690404): fmt, clippy with -D warnings, and the full test suite.

criteria.criterion: The new stop reason (if added) has a label and meaning and is listed wherever stops are enumerated (Stop::ALL, help text in crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs, display), verified by the existing test that every Stop has a meaning.
criteria.evidence: Stop::NeedsReinstall is added to Stop::ALL (now 9 entries) with the label `reinstall needed` and a meaning that mentions reinstalling. A new assertion checks that the meaning contains `reinstall`. The main.rs drain help text has the new line. `every_stop_reason_has_a_label_and_a_meaning` passed, and so did `drain_help_documents_the_flags_and_lists_every_stop_reason`, which runs the real binary.

findings.summary: If another worker has already set a stop, the reinstall stop and note are lost, and the job is still rated against the unreadable config.
findings.evidence: `set_stop` keeps only the first reason. In `finish`, rating is skipped only when `st.stop` is `NeedsReinstall`. Under `drain_concurrent`, if another worker has already set a reason (for example a stop request), `unreadable_config` is stored but never reported. Then `rate()` runs and reads the config this build cannot parse. A flag on State, such as `unreadable_config.is_some()`, would cover this case. Single-worker drains are not affected.

findings.summary: Any parse error in the landed config is treated as 'newer schema', so a job that simply breaks athena.toml also gets reinstall advice.
findings.evidence: The accepted reading allows this, and the code says so in comments. The note includes the parse error text, so the real cause stays visible.

findings.summary: I could not show that the real-steps test fails on the base tree.
findings.evidence: I am not allowed to change files, so I did not revert the fix and rerun the test. The stub tests cannot compile without the new Stop variant and Steps method, so at least those depend on the change.

summary: The change does what was asked. Straight after a successful landing, the drain now reads athena.toml at the new head. If this build cannot parse it, the job stays landed, rating and further items are skipped, and the run ends with a new stop, `reinstall needed`, plus a note giving the parse error and saying to reinstall and run `athena drain` again. If the same landing also rebuilt Athena, the run ends as `rebuilt` instead. I ran the new tests and they pass: a stub test, a real-steps test that commits an unknown section and checks the job record is Closed(Landed), and a rebuilt-case test. The repeated-failure regression test and the existing repeated-failure tests also pass, as do the stop label/meaning test and the drain --help test. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks pass. All changed files are on the deliverables list, and the CHANGELOG entry is clear and names the root cause. One minor gap: in a parallel drain where another worker has already set a stop, the reinstall stop is dropped and rating can still run against the unreadable config. That is not a blocker.
